page.title: Testing your charts · tinyactors guides
page.description: Test a chart's logic without its I/O and without waiting for its timeouts, with handlers your test writes and a simulated clock.

hero.headline: Test an hour of timeouts in milliseconds.
hero.lede: A test gives the host the I/O processors it wants and a clock that moves only when the test moves it. Then it reads a settled host after await host.idle().

section.heading: Three parts of the API make charts testable.

item.text: A test's handlers record what the chart sent and answer as the test decides: now, later, with an error, or never.

item.term: A SimulatedClock moves only when the test moves it.
item.text: A timeout of an hour takes no time.

item.term: await host.idle() returns when the host has nothing left to do.
item.text: The test then looks at a settled host.

section.p: For properties checked over generated runs instead of single cases, see .

section.heading: Check each step of a retrying payment.
section.p: This chart charges a card, retries when no answer comes within 30 seconds, and gives up after the third attempt. The test checks the sends, the state between them, and the end.

example.code: ok: retries, then gives up ok: an answer ends it

section.p: The test answered with payment.send('charged'), which is what the processor's send.answer('charged') does, without the sendid. A test may equally answer from the handler.

section.heading: Step to each deadline to see every tick.
section.p: clock.increment(ms) moves the clock once. What is due by then runs once, at the new time, and a delay it starts counts from the new time.
So a chart that ticks every second ticks once for an increment(3500), and its next tick is due a second later. host.nextDeadline says how far the next deadline is:

example.code: tick 1 at 3500 tick 2 at 4500 tick 3 at 5500 tick 4 at 6500

section.heading: Await idle between an input and a step.
section.p: host.send queues the event at once, but the actor handles it in the host's next turn, at the clock's time then. host.nextDeadline still reads the last idle turn's.
So an input followed by an increment in the same tick runs after the clock moved. A delay it starts counts from then:

example.code: nextDeadline right after the input: undefined reserved at 59000 reserved at 59000 expired at 119000 expired at 119000

section.p: Both holds came due at 119000, though the first was given at 0. Await idle() between the two when the input belongs before the step.

section.heading: On the real clock, wait for the assertion.
section.p: await host.idle() waits until the host has nothing to do now and no promise your handlers returned is pending. It waits for no deadline on the runtime's clock, nor a promise a handler starts without returning.
await actor.done settles when the actor reaches a top-level final state, with its <donedata>. await actor.ask(event, data) sends an event and settles with the chart's reply.

example.code: asked: progress 0 after idle(): still running done: all done

section.p: ask gives the event an origin the host answers itself. The chart replies with <send targetexpr="_event.origin">, as to another actor, and the promise settles with the reply's event name and data.
ask(event, data, { signal }) takes an AbortSignal. An aborted ask rejects with the signal's reason, and its reply, should one come, is dropped.
A host closed while an ask waits leaves it pending for ever, as it does a typed method's promise.

section.heading: Follow these habits in every test.

item.text: that should have an effect before the next assertion. A host runs on the event loop, so nothing has run right after actor.send returns.

item.term: Read state with the typed methods
item.text: actor.state() and actor.context(), after an idle(): they read the host as it is when called ().
to find them with host.actor(name), and to see that one ended: a final state ends the actor and frees its name, so host.actor(name) throws StaleError.
in a finally or the test framework's teardown. A host on a SimulatedClock arms no timer, so a forgotten one does not keep the process alive, but it holds its memory until collected.
if the charts will run on quickjs in production: give the host datamodel: 'quickjs' in a second run ().
with a snapshot: set a host up once, take host.snapshot(), and Host.restore it at the start of each test ().

item.term: Make an unhandled error fail the test.
item.text: A handler that throws is reported by the next await host.idle(), which rejects (Errors). A host given onHandlerError reports there instead: collect the errors and assert there are none.
